terms.meaning: The part a company plays on a project, such as owner, operator or EPC contractor.
A firm that engineers, buys equipment for and builds a plant.
A reference to the source document behind a number.

sections.name: File setup, SOURCE_TYPES
sections.title: Imports and source types for company details
sections.what: Brings in the company data calls, budget and capacity display helpers, citation pieces, login check and icons. Also defines the five source kinds.
sections.why: Likely reason: the page needs these to show the company, its projects and its citations.
sections.watch_out: The login check decides whether edit controls appear, so changing that hook changes who can edit.

sections.name: ROLE_LABELS
sections.title: Readable names for company roles
sections.what: Maps stored role codes, such as OWNER, OPERATOR and EPC, to the labels shown on the page. Unknown codes fall back to Other.
sections.why: Likely reason: stored codes are not friendly for readers, so each one gets a plain label.
sections.watch_out: A new role code needs an entry here, or it may not show as a readable name. The visible part does not show how unknown codes are handled beyond the Other label.

sections.name: STATUS_COLORS, ROLE_COLUMN, roleFieldPath
sections.title: Status colours and role evidence paths
sections.what: Maps each project status to the colour set used on its badge, such as green for on track and red for critical risk. Also maps each company role to the project fields that serve as evidence for it, and builds a comma-separated list of those fields for a given company.
sections.why: Likely reason: shared colours keep status badges consistent across pages, and the field list tells the evidence panel where to look for proof of a company's role.
sections.watch_out: A role missing from the role map produces only the company's own link path, so its evidence list may be short or empty.

sections.name: formatBudget
sections.title: Project budget text
sections.what: Returns the budget shown for a project as text. It uses the planned budget when one exists, falls back to the stated budget otherwise, and formats the amount with the project's industry and currency.
sections.why: Likely reason: one shared formatting rule keeps budget text the same wherever it appears.
sections.watch_out: Only the planned budget is checked first, so a project with both a planned and an actual budget shows only the planned one here.

sections.name: CompanyDetail (part 1)
sections.title: Page setup, editing state and profile save
sections.what: Starts the company page. It reads the company ID from the address, picks the correct back link for the industry, and checks whether the user is an admin. It loads the company and keeps an editable copy of its profile, which resets whenever the company data reloads.
sections.why: Likely reason: an editable copy keeps typing separate from the displayed data until the user saves.
sections.watch_out: The editable copy resets when company data reloads, so unsaved edits can be lost if the data refreshes while the user is typing.

sections.name: CompanyDetail (part 2)
sections.title: Alias, source and profile update actions
sections.what: Sets up the actions for adding and removing aliases, and for adding, switching, and removing sources. Also begins the profile save step, which rejects a blank name. Each action refreshes the company's data when it finishes.
sections.why: Likely reason: refreshing after each action lets the screen show the new state right away.
sections.watch_out: Only the profile save checks for a blank name in this section, so the other inputs depend on the server to reject bad values.

sections.name: CompanyDetail: if
sections.title: Website check, data loading and summary numbers
sections.what: Finishes the save step by checking that the website is a valid address. Then loads the company's linked projects, shows a spinner while loading, and shows Company not found if the company is missing. Works out the summary numbers for projects, total capacity, countries, and technologies, and builds the list of links to each project's page.
sections.why: Likely reason: the page checks for loading and missing data before drawing, so the summary numbers come only from loaded data.
sections.watch_out: The total capacity adds values measured on different bases, as the card label itself warns, so the total can mix units.

sections.name: CompanyDetail: for
sections.title: Evidence list builder and summary cards
sections.what: Builds the list of evidence items for a clicked summary card and opens it in the sources panel. Then draws the page heading and four summary cards for projects, reported capacity, countries, and technologies, each with a Sources button.
sections.why: Likely reason: each card has its own Sources button so users can check where its number comes from.
sections.watch_out: The project roles list counts every linking row, so a project with two roles can appear twice, while the other lists count each project once.

sections.name: CompanyDetail (part 5)
sections.title: Company info card and edit form start
sections.what: Draws the Company Info card header, with an Edit button that only admins see. In edit mode, it shows the name, type, country, and website fields.
sections.why: Likely reason: editing is limited to admins on this page, so other users see only the read-only view.
sections.watch_out: This hides the edit controls on the page only. The server must also refuse edits from non-admins, and that check is not visible in this code.

sections.name: CompanyDetail (part 6)
sections.title: Rest of edit form and buttons
sections.what: Shows the headquarters, founded, and description fields, any profile error, and the Cancel and Save Profile buttons. Cancel leaves edit mode and resets the fields to the saved values.
sections.why: Likely reason: Cancel resets the fields so discarded changes do not reappear the next time the form opens.
sections.watch_out: The website address is checked only when Save is pressed, not while the user types.

sections.name: CompanyDetail (part 7)
sections.title: Read-only company info view
sections.what: Shows the saved company details in a row of boxes: country, type, website as a link showing only the host name, headquarters, founded year, and roles. Shows the profile description below them when one exists.
sections.why: Likely reason: showing only the host name keeps long web addresses from crowding the layout.
sections.watch_out: The roles box is built from the roles found in linked projects, so a company with no linked projects shows no roles.

sections.name: CompanyDetail (part 8)
sections.title: Aliases card
sections.what: Lists the company's aliases as tags. Admins see an X on each tag to remove it, plus a box and Add button for a new alias, which also works when Enter is pressed. Shows a No aliases message when the list is empty.
sections.why: Likely reason: the add and remove controls are hidden from regular users, matching the admin-only edit rule.
sections.watch_out: Duplicate aliases are not checked in this section, so the same alias can be added twice unless the server rejects it.

sections.name: CompanyDetail (part 9)
sections.title: Sources card
sections.what: Lists the company's sources with their type, link, and status. Admins see a switch to turn each source on or off and a delete button. Other users see only On or Off text. Admins also get a type dropdown and a URL box for adding a source, which continue past this section.
sections.why: Likely reason: the status text tells regular users whether a source is active without offering controls.
sections.watch_out: The on and off switch and the delete button act right away, with no confirmation step.

sections.name: CompanyDetail (part 10)
sections.title: Add source form and role tables start
sections.what: Finishes the form where a user types a web address and clicks Add to attach a new source to the company. Then starts one card per role the company plays, each with a count and a table of its linked projects, showing the project name and a link to it.
sections.why: Likely reason: the page groups the company's projects by role so the user can see which projects the company works on in each role.
sections.watch_out: The Add button stays disabled until the address box has text, and it shows a spinner while the save is running.

sections.name: CompanyDetail (part 11)
sections.title: Project row details and empty message
sections.what: Fills the rest of each project row with country, technology, lifecycle stage, status, capacity and budget. Missing values show a grey not-available label. Most values can be clicked to open their source citation. If the company has no linked projects, a message says so.
sections.why: Likely reason: each value can be traced to its source, so the page offers a citation for each one.
sections.watch_out: Each citation key names a field such as status or capacityValue. If a key does not match the real field name, the citation can point to the wrong data.

sections.name: CompanyDetail (part 12)
sections.title: Geographic and technology summary cards
sections.what: Shows two summary cards at the bottom. One lists each country where the company has projects, with the project count. The other lists each technology with its project count. A card is hidden when it has nothing to show.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives a quick overview of where the company works and what it builds.
sections.watch_out: The counts appear to come only from the projects already loaded on this page, so they may not cover every project the company has.

summary: The detail page for one company: shows its profile, its projects with roles, and its sources, with editing controls for signed-in users.
purpose: Lets someone review and edit a single company and see which projects it is part of.
why: Likely reason: the page combines a company's facts and its project links in one view. Only two sections were visible, so the wider reason is not confirmed.
how: 1. Reads the company id from the page address. 2. Loads the company and its projects. 3. Shows the profile with readable role labels. 4. Shows edit controls, likely only to signed-in users. 5. Opens citations for values through the sources panel.
inputs: The company id from the address, the company record and project list from the server, and the login state.
outputs: A profile view, a list of projects with roles and budgets, and edit actions.
risks: Only 2 of 16 sections were available to review. Edit actions depend on the login hook. A role code missing from the label list may not display as readable text.
debug: If a role name looks odd, check the role label list. If the page is blank, check the company id in the address and the company request. If edit controls are missing, check the login state.
